title: Volume-normalized mid-expiratory flow fails to improve transported wheeze prediction beyond standard spirometry
abstract: Mid-expiratory flow may contain respiratory information beyond FEV1 and FVC, but incremental clinical usefulness remains disputed. We registered a test of log(FEF25–75/FVC), a volume-normalized timing representation, for concurrent past-year wheeze. Survey-weighted logistic models were trained in 3712 NHANES2007–2008 adults and frozen before evaluation in 3691 separately sampled NHANES2011–2012 adults. Beyond FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC, demographics, body size and smoking, the feature changed target weighted Brier from 0.097321 to 0.097467; delta+0.000146, approximate target-PSU95% interval[+0.000040,+0.000255], joint-refit interval[-0.000186,+0.000659]. AUC changed by-0.000299. Flexible baseline and measurement-quality restrictions also showed no point improvement. This negative transport test does not establish absence of small-airway physiology, equivalence, or a universal lack of usefulness of mid-expiratory flow. Shared survey protocols and cross-sectional self-report limit generalizability.
